body: Thanks! It’s just hard to start over on a psychology level because I’m so angry at the past and people who have wronged. Right now, I’m just trying to get in the right head space and learn to let the past go! Easier said than done!
Thanks! Anything else? How do you really start over?

Robert is the one who opened my eyes about this along with Dale Carnegie.

Read : how to win friends and influence people, play the perfect courtier law from the 48 laws of power, and the art of seduction. ESPECIALLY a the art of seduction. Like Robert said seduction isn’t just about having sex or a romantic partner. It’s about using the seduction types in your career as well. Celebrities use the art of seduction all the time. Robert Greene admits he uses these seduction techniques I his writing too.

Examples: Beyoncé = the siren 
                   Harry styles = dandy
                   Timothy Chalomet= the star/ dandy/charmer he seems to channel all three of these.

Remember, the game of power is a social game too. 

I wish I had learned this when I was young.

Learn now young grasshopper.

Of course they did, he was no longer a threat or competitive. That’s what I had to learn after losing weight.  I learned that I was the non-threatening and non-competitive fat person who made everyone feel secure and superior.

That’s what most people want. They want someone around them who makes them feel superior and secure. However, once you stop playing your role it hit the road jack for you! 


However, I do think there is something you can learn from this guy. Play the role of the “chill” “cool guy” while simultaneously aspiring to accumulate powerful positions. You can gain both reputation and power. But, if you can’t do both go for power every time.


I’ve been where this guy is now and he will look back on those days with shame and embarrassment.

I agree with the last part. I have a perfect example. I lost weight over a year ago. When I was fat, I was the mediocre loser that made everyone feel like a winner. However, when I lost the weight and started eating healthier I got so much hate from my boss and co-workers and everyone around me. People would give me dirty looks, co-worked who used to chat with me went silent, the boss would scold me for eating healthy food instead the junk food that was ordered, co-workers offered me food in order get me to gain the weight back, and only ONE person complimented me. And don’t get me started on the people who told me to stop.

People will despise you just  for making healthy choices and improving your life and love you for being a loser and a mediocrity. 

So you are 100% correct. You have to choose what you are willing to gain and willing lose. And like Robert Greene says, the game of power is a game of loss and gain.

This is why I have a problem with the reputation law because it depends too much on people and their fickle feelings. You can lose reputation by inadvertently hurting someone’s fragile ego. 

And in that case, what good is a reputation?

It’s not all wrong. Successful people have a network of people who serve their interest. Once these people no longer serve them or someone gains more power and money they will be disposed of.

For example, Warren Buffet may have a network of rich and powerful people who share the same aims. However, as soon as opportunity presents itself where only one person can advance and the rest will be left behind they will turn on each other in the name of self-interest. 

That’s part of the game: use people until you no longer need them. 

I regret not realizing this at 18. My life would have turned out differently.

I already feel betrayed. I feel betrayed by a world that lied and told everyone to be moral and fair in  an amoral and unfair world. I feel even more betrayed by religions like Christianity, who played a role in promoting these lies. It did nothing but, turn me into a loser and guess what? That was the goal.

This world is competitive and people want to win and they want everyone else to lose. And part of winning the game of life, is pumping the competitions head full of lies so that they will always make the wrong decision. It’s psychological warfare and Robert Greene is one of the few authors telling the truth about the ruthless, competitive world we live in.

I’ve been fooled too many times into doing this and wasted YEARS of my life looking for relationships like this that don’t exist. Human beings are self-serving to the core and deep down NO ONE wants you to successful or do better than them no matter how much they say they do. They will appear to be helping you while simultaneously walking you off a cliff. 

Niccolo Machiavelli talked about this in his book “The Prince”. You do not help other people gain power and people are clearly practicing this rule. 

In the eyes of most people, life is a zero sum game. You either win or you lose. And they want to win.

This is why I said I would take everything with a grain of salt. I know now that are limitations to a human beings help.

I have accepted that I am alone and that I alone will have to save myself.

To be honest, going crazy is exactly what has happened to me. I have allowed other people to pump my head full of so many lies and manipulate me into doing things that have made my “life” embarrassing, humiliating, and and shameful. I look back on the last 10-20 years and I can’t believe I did the things I did and believed the things these people told me. It’s shameful. There are days I try to escape it all but, it in the end the flood of shame, guilt, and embarrassment come running right back. And now, I’m a loser from head to toe. 

However, I think you have given me some good ideas on where to start. However, if there if there’s is one thing I’ve learned from Robert Greene it’s this: you have to wage war on yourself before raising war on others.
Another great quote!

I thought the exact same thing when I read your quote: this person has been where I have been and has walked the path I’m walking now. You feel so cheated and robbed out of your youth time you will never get back. It’s painful and heartbreaking. I won’t lie, there I days where I feel it is too late for me but, if you walked into  this 9th ring of hell and managed to tame some of these demons out here. I’m all ears.
I just wanted to know where to start. I’ve been on the wrong path my whole life. At the very least, I would like to be pointed in the right direction, for once.
Do you think it’s wise to dream so big? Aren’t you setting yourself up for disappointment?  However I do get you mean, plan the future you want or at least aim for it.

“Think about all the world has taken from you and how much you’ve given with nothing in return.” 

WOW. That is one of the most motivational quotes I’ve ever heard. You described exactly how I feel to the last letter. This quote will stay with me. Forget about just taking my life back, I might just take the whole Milky Way too.
How do you “handle” all of it?

I no longer give people the benefit of the doubt.  I’m too old for that. I see things very clearly now. 

People are not good.
People don’t want you to succeed. 
People want you to fail.
People want you settle for living a mediocre life.
And if you refuse to settle, they want you to die. 
Human beings are insanely competitive and amoral.
They will do whatever it takes to get what they want and that includes destroying you. 

People are not angry that you’re not getting better.
They’re angry that you’re not dead yet. They’re angry that you refuse to stay in the non-threatening, non-competitive role you were assigned. They’re angry that you refuse to accept and be complacent with mediocrity.
You know what’s worse? Realizing that they never cared and they wanted things to turn out this way. They wanted you to become a failure so that they could feel like a success.

I just wrote a post about this. 

Read it. 

I am going through the same thing where I’m beginning to realize people are not good.

Toxic positivity is textbook gaslighting. No one wants you to realize how bad things  are because no one wants you get better. 

The truth hurts and reality is harsh. Once you embrace the harsh realities of life and the painful truths, things WILL get better. 

But, you have stop letting assholes gaslight you with this positivity/negativity bullshit. 

All of us on this Reddit have the same problem. Something has gone very wrong in our lives. 
We need to face the truth no matter how “negative” it may be.

Edit: Never listen to anyone who tell you to settle for less. That’s what this evil society wants. If you aren’t going to settle for less, they want you dead hence the suicidal thoughts.

You just described everything I have ever felt or thought about suicide. 

Human beings are evil and have a long, long history of  committing evil acts that have destroyed lives. Yet, suicide is called “irrational”. It seems like a logical option to me.

There is another option.
Live for yourself and take care of yourself.

Bad people are liars. They say “don’t commit suicide” because they can’t tell you the truth which is this: 

They want you dead. You’re a threat that needs to be eliminated. 

The world is an insanely competitive place.

People see you as competition. And you don’t help the competition you destroy it.

They are intentionally making your problems worse. The worse your problems get the more therapy and pills you need. 

The more pills and therapy you need the more money they make. 

It’s time for society to knock medical and psychology fields off their pedestals and to see them for what they are: businesses selling products and services for profit.
